purpose: Choose one mechanism-independent deterministic Alpha158 cross-operator agreement factor for Campaign294 without reading Campaign294 candidate values, comparator values, daily prices or forward returns.

finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.name: alpha158_same_horizon_cross_family_peer_rank_consensus_5h
finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.reason: The Alpha158 horizon grid is a fixed 29-operator by five-horizon matrix. Campaign293 measured along rows, comparing horizons within one operator. The transposed mechanism measures continuous cross-operator agreement within each fixed horizon and removes the common percentile level through population variance.

parameters.peer_percentile: (ascending average-tie rank - 0.5) / finite model-support peer count
parameters.per_horizon_dispersion: population variance across finite operator-family peer percentiles
parameters.score: 1 - 4 * equal-weight mean of the five per-horizon population variances

finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.name: alpha158_same_horizon_cross_family_peer_rank_dispersion_5h
finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.reason: Raw dispersion is a deterministic affine inversion of the selected consensus score and is not a second independent direction.

finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.name: alpha158_cross_family_iqr_mad_pairwise_gap_or_entropy_grid
finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.reason: IQR, MAD, pairwise absolute gaps, entropy and trimmed variance would open an avoidable aggregation-family search around the same cross-operator disagreement hypothesis.

finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.name: alpha158_horizon_specific_or_horizon_weighted_cross_family_consensus
finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.reason: Selecting one horizon or fitting short-versus-long horizon weights would create a five-way subset and weighting search; all five frozen horizons retain equal weight.

finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.name: alpha158_cross_family_common_peer_rank_level
finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.reason: A common percentile mean would primarily recover technical level or extremity already represented by the Alpha158 coordinate library and Campaign292. Population variance deliberately removes the common level.

finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.name: alpha158_family_subset_or_support_threshold_grid
finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.reason: Operator subsets and support sweeps would add multiplicity. Every one of the 29 named families is admitted, every horizon must have at least the single frozen 75-percent floor of 22 finite families, and all five horizons must qualify.

finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.name: campaign290_to_campaign293_retune_inversion_or_combination
finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.reason: All four prior Alpha158 directions remain terminal and may appear only as frozen duplicate-control comparators; they may not be inverted, thresholded, reweighted, combined or rescued.

finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.name: alpha158_supervised_tree_mlp_kernel_or_hash_model_refresh
finite_prevalue_concept_catalog.reason: Campaign286-289 already consumed those frozen supervised or randomized model mechanisms. Campaign294 is a single deterministic no-fit factor.

selected_formula.name: alpha158_same_horizon_cross_family_peer_rank_consensus_5h
selected_formula.formula: For each accepted session t and Alpha158 coordinate j in the 29 frozen five-horizon families, rank finite model-support peers with ascending average ties and set u_tij=(rank-0.5)/finite_peer_count. For each stock i and each horizon h, collect the 29 same-horizon family percentiles and require at least 22 finite values. All five horizons must qualify. Compute the population variance v_tih across finite operator families for each horizon, then score 1-4*mean_h(v_tih). Do not use the 13 non-horizon coordinates; do not fill, clip, sign, threshold, weight, fit, invert, subset or combine the score.
selected_formula.economic_hypothesis: When many distinct technical operators place a stock at similar peer-relative positions over the same lookback, its technical state is cross-operator coherent rather than driven by one isolated indicator and may persist from the next open through the third close.

mechanism_separation.campaign290: No prior session, lag, suspension bridge or state-persistence count is used.
mechanism_separation.campaign291: No below/equal/above-median ternary state or modal-state fraction is used; Campaign294 measures continuous variance separately inside each fixed horizon.
mechanism_separation.campaign292: No mean absolute distance from the peer median is used; common high or low percentile level cancels from population variance.
mechanism_separation.campaign293: Campaign293 compares horizons within each operator family; Campaign294 uses the transposed axis, comparing operator families within each horizon, with no adjacent-horizon difference.
mechanism_separation.campaign286_to_campaign289: No return-supervised fit, tree, neural network, random Fourier feature or hash cell is used.
